book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: In such a heated environment, poor poker resources get exposed

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the following words are knocked out of their proper order

parts.note: the fourteen letters of these two words are the fodder
surface padding: completes the picture of a player's chips laid bare and gives no letters

explanation.surface: A card player under stress at the table sees their dwindling stack of chips laid bare.
explanation.walkthrough: Poker resources are chips, which fits the gambling picture; 'get exposed' rounds off the surface and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressure cooker is a sealed pot that cooks with steam, and figuratively any tense, high-stress situation.

clue.text: State formed by amalgamating Virginia and Vermont?

parts.words: State formed by amalgamating Virginia and Vermont?
parts.note: surface reading: a new US state made by merging two existing ones
setter's reading: 'state' is the verb meaning to declare firmly

explanation.surface: A political fantasy about merging two eastern US states into one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' is a verb, not a territory. The mention of Virginia and Vermont looks like a play on their postal codes VA and VT, but no clean way to build the answer from them has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something as true, a formal synonym of the verb to state.

clue.text: Verbally expressed degree of confidence won't have me restricting it

indicators.note: the pronoun me hems the rest in on both sides, and the clue says to do without that enclosing pair

parts.note: morale is a group's level of confidence and spirit

explanation.surface: Someone declines to let a colleague limit how sure the team sounds when it speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: MORALE begins with M and ends with E, so ME wraps round the middle; take that pair away and four letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Oral means spoken rather than written, which is what verbally expressed describes.

clue.text: Top one on horse is amongst the all-time greats

indicators.note: to be amongst a group is to sit inside it, so the rider and mount go within the next phrase

parts.note: the all-time greats are the best ever
Roman numeral one
gee-gee, a childish word for a horse

explanation.surface: A champion jockey on a famous horse earns a place among the sport's legends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top one' looks like a single phrase for the champion, but 'Top' alone is the definition and 'one on horse' is a rider sitting on GG.
explanation.definitionFit: Biggest and top both mean the leading or greatest of all, as in the top or biggest name in the sport.

clue.text: Make more time: £1000 is to be invested

indicators.note: money that is invested is put into something, so the sum goes inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction for buying extra time: put a thousand pounds into the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes 'Make more time' look like the definition, but 'time' belongs to the wordplay. The answer takes the British -ISE spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrandise is to increase the size, power or importance of something, to make it greater.

clue.text: Lie about young woman having implant of German synthetic material

indicators.note: an implant is something placed inside, so the abbreviation is set within the string of words

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
re means about or concerning
G is the abbreviation for German
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Gossip about a young woman who has had a cosmetic implant made of artificial material.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests surgery, but the implant is the single letter for German slipped between the young woman and what comes before her.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibreglass is a man-made composite of glass fibres set in resin, used for boat hulls and insulation.

clue.text: Warning that 2011 might split, for example?

definitions.text: Warning that 2011 might split, for example?

parts.note: surface reading: a prediction that the year might break apart
setter's reading: a lamp on the back of a car that warns others the driver is backing up

explanation.surface: A doom-laden forecast that the year 2011 might fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's '2011' is probably a cross-reference to entries 20 and 11, whose answers read backwards from words; 'light' is crossword jargon for an entry, so those are reversing lights in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversing light is the white lamp on a vehicle's rear that comes on to warn others it is going backwards.

clue.text: One pursuing quarry aims to give him this power in game

indicators.note: giving him something places it inside him, so the phrase goes inside the word for the pursuer

parts.note: a hunter is one who pursues prey
what the hunted animal wants to give its pursuer is the slip, an escape
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A hunted animal tries to outwit the hunter on its trail and gain the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone the slip is to escape them: the quarry aims to give the hunter THE SLIP, and that phrase plus P goes inside him. Hunt the slipper is a parlour game in which players search for a hidden shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunt the slipper is a traditional children's party game in which a shoe is passed secretly round a circle while one player seeks it.

clue.text: I look forward to reading things up …

definitions.text: I look forward to reading things up …

parts.words: I look forward to reading things up
parts.note: surface reading: someone eager to do some research
setter's reading: one who reads the things up above, the stars and planets, in order to look forward into the future

explanation.surface: An eager student says they are keen to do some background reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look forward to' seems to mean enjoy in advance, and 'reading up' seems to mean studying; in fact the speaker foretells the future from the heavens overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer claims to forecast events by interpreting the positions of the stars and planets in the sky.

clue.text: Confess with leg restrained

indicators.note: something restrained is held in, so the short word holds the abbreviation captive

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is also called the on side
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A suspect owns up while their leg is held down or shackled.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg side and on side are the same half of the field, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: To own, or own up to, something is to admit or confess it.

clue.text: … or writing about town in Nevada where people are divided

definitions.text: town in Nevada where people are divided

parts.note: surface reading: a place of political or social division
setter's reading: the Nevada city famous for quick divorces, where couples are legally parted
surface padding: continues the ellipsis from 9 across, as if the astrologer also writes

explanation.surface: The ellipsis continues 9 across, as if the astrologer also writes up a divided Nevada town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divided' suggests factions, but it means divorced: Nevada's short residency rule made this city the divorce capital of America.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno, Nevada, became world-famous in the twentieth century for its easy, fast divorces, splitting married couples apart.

clue.text: 3's nearly over 27

indicators.note: in an across clue, turned over means the letters are flipped round to run the other way
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: 3 down is ORAL, and an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A terse cross-reference clue with no real story of its own.
explanation.walkthrough: Both numbers point at other answers: 3 down is ORAL, which leads to EXAM, and 27 down is CHOP, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To chop is to cut with heavy blows, and to axe is to cut down or chop with an axe.

clue.text: Hold English hero with both arms, taking everything in?

parts.note: something full has taken in all it can hold
Admiral Lord Nelson, the English naval hero of Trafalgar
surface padding that also describes the hold, which is applied with both arms

explanation.surface: A tribute to a national hero embracing the whole crowd in a two-armed hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With both arms' describes the hold: a full nelson uses both arms under the opponent's armpits, unlike a half nelson. Nelson is the admiral on the column in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: A full nelson is a wrestling grip in which both arms lock behind an opponent's neck from below the armpits.

clue.text: Sinister chap deserted the wife and shacked up?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sinister is Latin for left, the heraldic term for the left side

definitions.text: chap deserted the wife and shacked up?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a ... marriage is an irregular or morganatic union, and the man has left the wife for it

explanation.surface: A shady man walked out on his wife to live with someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' reads as menacing, but here it is its Latin root, left. The second half plays on 'left' (deserted) and 'handed' (given in marriage) for an informal union.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister originally meant on the left side, so it is an old synonym for left-handed; a left-handed marriage is an irregular one.

clue.text: Group exploding myth during cruise abroad

indicators.note: during places one thing in the course of another, so the first set of letters goes inside the second
an explosion scatters things, so the letters of the word that follows are blown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged too

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A band of tourists debunks a legend while on a holiday cruise overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is a pop group: the 1980s British duo of Annie Lennox and Dave Stewart.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurythmics were a British pop duo, a musical group famous for 'Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)'.

clue.text: Number attending denouement of scandal

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the attendance figure at a sports match
second meaning: the suffix that ends the names of scandals, after Watergate

explanation.surface: A crowd turns up for the final act of a public scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: Ever since Watergate, scandals have been named with this word on the end, as in Partygate, so it is literally the end of a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is the number of spectators at a match, and -gate is the suffix tacked on to name political scandals.

clue.text: Do a class

parts.note: per means a or each, as in ten pounds per head
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: A short instruction to take or teach a lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is PER, as in twice a day, twice per day; form is the British school word for a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform is to do or carry out, as in perform a task, so do substitutes for it.

clue.text: Keep misconstruing dialect

indicators.note: misconstruing means interpreting wrongly, so the following word is read with its letters in a wrong order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone keeps misunderstanding a regional way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep' looks like a verb meaning continue, but it is the noun for the stronghold at the heart of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the strongest inner tower of a castle, and a citadel is a fortress protecting a town.

clue.text: Fond of food, boy gorges it

indicators.note: to gorge is to stuff food down inside oneself, so the boy takes the food into his middle

parts.note: a son is a boy
tuck is British school slang for food, especially sweets and snacks

explanation.surface: A greedy boy who loves his grub wolfs it down.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is old British public-school slang for snacks and sweets, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuck on is an informal idiom for being keen on or infatuated with someone or something.

clue.text: Bear to ring back

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the word is read from its end

parts.note: a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: An instruction to phone someone back about a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like a verb meaning tolerate, and 'ring back' like a phone call; in fact the bear is a famous fictional one.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh is A. A. Milne's honey-loving teddy, perhaps the best-known bear in children's books.

clue.text: Checks Cinderella's post-midnight garb?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a woollen check pattern of thin lines on a light ground
second meaning, read as two words: after midnight her ballgown is gone and her clothes are ... of them

explanation.surface: A question about what Cinderella wears once the clock strikes twelve and the magic ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Checks' seems to be a verb, but it is a cloth pattern; the second half splits the answer as tatters + all, Cinderella's rags.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattersall is a check fabric pattern, named after the London horse market whose blankets used it.

clue.text: Ethiopian prince spots hospital off headland

indicators.note: off means removed, so the letter for the hospital is taken away

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots
H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An African royal with a skin complaint is kept away from a clinic on a cape.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is defined twice: it is an Ethiopian title of nobility, and an Arabic word for a cape that appears in place names such as Ras Tanura.
explanation.definitionFit: Ras is the title of an Ethiopian prince or duke, and in Arabic geography it names a cape or headland.

clue.text: The tree remains

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a common hardwood tree
second meaning: the powdery residue left after burning

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests whatever is left of a felled tree; the two halves are unrelated meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a familiar deciduous tree, and ash is also what is left after a fire, including cremated remains.

clue.text: Hide in quizmaster's seat (nude)?

parts.note: surface reading: a naked person sitting in the quiz show chair
setter's reading: an animal's pelt, the leather of the seat and also what a nude sits in

explanation.surface: A streaker hides in the famous quiz chair with nothing on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb meaning conceal, but it is the noun for an animal pelt; someone nude is in their bare covering, and the quiz chair is upholstered in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hide and skin are synonyms for the pelt of an animal, especially when treated as leather.

clue.text: Seeing Little and Large in road, credit impersonation

parts.note: surface reading: the British comedy double act of Syd Little and Eddie Large
setter's reading: an instrument that lets you see something little as if it were large
the rest of the clue as printed; its wordplay has not been worked out

explanation.surface: A fan spots the comedy duo Little and Large on the road doing their impression act.
explanation.walkthrough: Little and Large were a British TV comedy double act of the 1970s and 80s. The rest of the clue reads as wordplay that has not been fully worked out.
explanation.definitionFit: A microscope magnifies tiny objects, so the viewer sees little things enlarged.

clue.text: Shirt can't cover upper body roughly

indicators.note: what cannot cover is missing from the top of a down answer, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the torso is the trunk of the body
a T-shirt, and the letter T that names it

explanation.surface: A shirt too small to cover someone's chest, give or take.
explanation.walkthrough: The T of T-shirt is the letter at the top of the trunk word, and it is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Or so is an idiom meaning approximately, as in ten minutes or so.

clue.text: A blow promptly repeated

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sharp downward stroke, as in karate
second meaning: said twice it is a call to hurry up

explanation.surface: A punch thrown again without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chop-chop!' is an informal call meaning quickly, so the word repeated means promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop is a short downward blow, and the doubled form chop-chop is slang for quickly.

clue.text: With it kids got over "Instructions on How to Register Eco-Vote"?

parts.note: green means environmentally friendly
a voter marks the ballot with a cross
a code is a set of rules or instructions

explanation.surface: A cool youth crowd skims a pamphlet on how to cast an environmental vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With it' seems to mean fashionable, but 'it' is the answer: the road-safety code helped children get over the road. The Green Cross Code is the UK's pedestrian safety rules for children.
explanation.definitionFit: The Green Cross Code is the British road-safety routine taught to children for crossing the street safely.
